content.text: -    MOA: H1-receptor antagonist (1st-gen, cross BBB) -> block CNS his wakefulness -> sedation (+ anticholinergic)
-    1st-gen: also brompheniramine, chlorpheniramine, clemastine (cross BBB → sedation + antimuscarinic)

-    2nd-gen: cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine, desloratadine, levocetirizine (⍉cross BBB → less sedation + ⍉antimuscarinic); use: allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis, urticaria, atopy, eczema, food + drug allergy, hay fever
-    Clin Use: allergy sx (runny nose, sneezing, itchy/watery eyes, throat itching) · common cold sx (adults only) · insomnia (OTC sedative; may help initiate sleep; tolerance develops)

-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w EToH/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)
-    Toxicity: antimuscarinic + H1 block + Na-channel block → anticholinergic syndrome, sedation, sz/dysrhythmia
-    MOA: phenothiazine H1 antagonist (+ D2 block -> antiemetic) -> sedation + anticholinergic
-    Caution: ↓ sz threshold · CI comatose states, phenothiazine hypersensitivity/idiosyncratic rxn
-    BBW: potentially fatal resp depression · CI <2 y (peds ≥2 y: use w caution)

-    Herpes labialis (recurr): acyclovir, famciclovir, or valacyclovir; topical penciclovir or docosanol; prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) if ≥6 outbreaks/yr
-    HSV keratitis: acyclovir eye drops, or PO therapy
-    acyclovir: HSV, herpes zoster, varicella; ⍉active vs influenza A or B
